content: Palmoplantar keratoderma (PPK), also known as keratosis palmaris et plantaris, is a dermatological condition that primarily affects the skin of the palms and soles. It is characterized by a marked thickening of the skin in these areas. The etiology of PPK can be classified into three categories: hereditary, acquired, or as a manifestation of another underlying disease where PPK is an associated feature. Diagnosis of PPK involves a thorough physical examination of the skin. Visual inspection typically reveals the characteristic thickened skin on the palms and soles. Specific patterns, such as marginal keratoderma or progressive forms of palmoplantar keratoderma, may be observed. These findings are often documented and referenced with permission from dermatological atlases to ensure accurate identification and classification of the condition.
